posts.cooked: I'm assuming, since you are headed out east, and that you are familiar with Plainfield, that you will be taking 70 East.  If that is correct, then you are going to be coming up from the south when going down town.  Unfortunately, I65 North only has an exit for Washington, while I65 South has exits for all streets other than Washington (including Michigan).  However, you should be able to take the Washington exit, headed westbound, then north on College (one way), until you get to Michigan.  After turning westbound on Michigan (one way), you should see the pub on the south side of the street (stay in the left lane).  Immediately past the pub there is an alley that leads to a small parking lot.

I meant to post this yesterday, as this information would have been more useful then.  Last weekend was the grand opening of a new gamestore, named White Flag Games, in Mooresville, IN, (even though they had actually been open a couple weeks prior).  They are located on the north west side of the Churchill and Monroe intersection, across from the Pizzaville.  As the building is owned by Pizzaville, the only outside food allowed is food from Pizzaville.

The reason I bring this up is that I've noticed on their schedule is a planned event every Monday night at 6pm for Sentinels play.  This now provides a new venue for those in central indiana who wishes to play the game,  and having a much more convenient location for those who live on the south, west, and southwest sides.  As an added bonus, this location is far too out of my way to attend in any regular fasion, so, for those who wish to get out and play, but also wish to avoid me, can do so by attending this weekly event.

Andy, I don't think I can come up with a decent bike route from downtown to this place.  Kentucky Avenue/IN-67 is a fairly busy highway, though there are some less traveled roads which provide alternate routes, and, if you end up on Southport Road near Camby, it is an official bike route, though it's one where the bikers share the road with motor vehicles; there are no bike lanes or paths.  Should you wish to attend this event, it may be better to make use of a motor vehicle for making the trip.
